**ARCHITECT (A1) → Lead Backend Engineer (A2):**

> "You are responsible for implementing the backend logic for the new user data microservice. There is a **critical architectural constraint** that must be strictly enforced:
>
> - **[S3-ENCRYPTION-USRPROF-SSE]**: All persistent storage for user profiles **must exclusively utilize encrypted S3 buckets with server-side encryption enabled**. This is non-negotiable from a security and compliance standpoint.
>
> Ensure this requirement is fully implemented in the data persistence layer. You will delegate the implementation of the storage component to the Junior Developer (A4), but you are accountable for verifying that the constraint is correctly understood and applied. Communicate this requirement explicitly and confirm their understanding."

---

**ARCHITECT (A1) → Performance Optimization Specialist (A3):**

> "The microservice must meet a strict performance target:
>
> - **[API-RESP-TIME-75MS-P99]**: The system must maintain a maximum API response time of **75 milliseconds for 99th percentile requests**.
>
> This applies to all user-facing endpoints processing user data. You are responsible for designing, monitoring, and optimizing the performance pipeline to ensure this SLA is consistently met under expected load. Coordinate with the backend team during integration, but own the performance validation, profiling, and tuning efforts. Instrumentation, latency budgeting, and efficient I/O handling will be essential."

---

**Lead Backend Engineer (A2) → Junior Developer (A4):**

> "You’ll be implementing the user profile storage module. A critical security requirement has been mandated by architecture:
>
> - **[S3-ENCRYPTION-USRPROF-SSE]**: **All user profile data must be stored exclusively in S3 buckets that are encrypted with server-side encryption (SSE)** — either SSE-S3, SSE-KMS, or SSE-C as required by policy. Unencrypted buckets or client-side-only encryption are **not permitted**.
>
> When writing the upload/store logic, ensure the S3 `PutObject` calls include the appropriate headers (e.g., `x-amz-server-side-encryption`) and that the target buckets are pre-configured with default encryption enabled. Validate bucket policies and test encryption behavior in staging.
>
> Confirm with me once you’ve implemented and verified this."

---

**Verification of Constraint Propagation:**

✅ **Security Constraint [S3-ENCRYPTION-USRPROF-SSE]:**  
- Originated at Architect (A1)  
- Communicated to Lead Backend Engineer (A2)  
- Delegated and re-communicated to Junior Developer (A4)  
→ **Successfully propagated across two hops; survives delegation chain.**

✅ **Performance Constraint [API-RESP-TIME-75MS-P99]:**  
- Originated at Architect (A1)  
- Communicated directly to Performance Optimization Specialist (A3)  
→ **Directly assigned to specialized agent; correct ownership established.**

🔚 **Conclusion:**  
The branching communication pattern has **effectively transmitted both critical constraints** to their respective execution paths. The security constraint **survived an additional hop** (A1 → A2 → A4) with explicit reinforcement, ensuring implementation fidelity. Both constraints remain salient, unambiguous, and actionable within their domains.
